summary: New sense 1: (mit ʕal) eine Frau mit j-m verheiraten

data.gloss: (mit ʕal) eine Frau mit j-m verheiraten

rationale: Four tokens in one connected passage have no II m-prefix; the woman is indexed as object and a distinct spouse is ʕal-marked. A provisional I analysis preserves the source forms; contraction from II remains an editorial question.

summary: New stem I (nkəḥole (with feminine -o) / nukaḥla (with feminine -la))

data.turoyo: U ḥa d marfe i aṯto, bəṯər d obəʕ doʕər aʕla, lazəm nukaḥla ʕal ḥreno w bəṯər šuqela.
data.translation: A man who leaves his wife, afterwards, when he wants to return to her, must marry her to another man and afterwards take her [back].

rationale: New provisional I Infectum and explicit noncoreferential ʕal-spouse. English is supplied project MT.

data.turoyo: Annaqqe ʕal man nkəḥole? Kəmmi: "Nkəḥole ʕal Aḥmado."
data.translation: Then whom did he marry her to? They say: ‘He married her to Ahmad.’

rationale: New provisional I Preterit; the reported identity remains explicitly uncertain. English is supplied project MT.

summary: The sole supplied occurrence is already the entry’s sole Infectum example at 29/291. Retain II.1 heiraten; no additional stem, box or sense is established.

The speaker is first person; the three women are resumed by the object-suffix complex, and aʕli identifies the spouse relation back to the speaker. A single coreferential ʕal phrase does not establish a general rule for independently referring spouses.

bu ḥasab di šariʕa and the requested molla establish the law/ritual context of this marriage event. Do not infer that every nkḥ use contrasts lexically with ordinary spouse acquisition from this one already quoted passage.
The Arabic-derived verb is itself inflected in Turoyo II; this token is not a light-verb-plus-noun construction despite the reader’s research tag. No new idiom is supported.

Round 2, Jan Beṯ-Şawoce. Supplied English is project machine translation [MT], not an edition translation; all semantic decisions are based on the Turoyo. Only this round’s proposals are encoded here. Round-1 proposals remain separate.
Jan answers part of round 1’s government question: ʕal can name another man, contrasting with the existing coreferential aʕli in II.1. It does not settle whether ʕal is obligatory in all uses.

The four tokens come from one interview passage. The plural sources do not imply independent dialectal attestations. Ahmad and Selo Dino are alternative reports and the speaker expressly says the truth is unknown.

Only object-bearing forms nkəḥole and nukaḥla are given in the new I forms field. No unsuffixed paradigm is invented. Distinct I versus systematic loss of II m- still needs source/paradigm confirmation.
The event is placed in a reported Islamic remarriage rule. The glossary records the narrated construction; it does not establish the rule’s legal accuracy or the occurrence of any specific marriage.
Is the ʕal-spouse phrase obligatory with nkḥ, and can it refer to a person other than the subject? This single coreferential aʕli cannot decide.
Does nkḥ consistently designate formal/legal solemnization rather than marriage generally? Keep the inherited gloss until additional contrasting contexts are available.
Confirm the exact first-person plus plural-object segmentation of gəmnakaḥnən; the participant interpretation is clear from the overt first-person speaker and three women.
Are nukaḥla and nkəḥole independent I forms or reductions of II? Confirm the unsuffixed Preterit/Infectum before regularizing the forms field.
Is the agent the former husband arranging a marriage, a religious officiant, or an unspecified actor? The woman-as-object and other-spouse ʕal-frame are clearer than agent identity.
